title: The Azarian Peaks Expedition
dek: Liora leads the company into the Unwelcoming Peaks to seek Vasatzi’s scattered artifacts. Questions about saving her become urgent as the mountains break around them.

facts.People: Leo; Gudlaug; Olokun; Liora Fenwick; Scribonia; Eugene; Dex Corbin; Uthgar

body:
After a difficult sea crossing, the company reaches a rocky shore beneath the snow-covered Azarian Peaks. Thunder rolls inside the mountains and the ground shakes as they approach Liora Fenwick. The young half-elf scholar has been waiting for them. She knows the route into the peaks, and she has asked them here because she believes someone within them can still be helped.

The recorded company includes Leo, Gudlaug, Olokun, Scribonia and Eugene, with Dex Corbin and Uthgar also directly present in the encounter. Their first task is to understand what Liora is asking before committing themselves to the climb.

Liora’s request

Liora calls the mountains the Unwelcoming Peaks and interprets their disturbances through the prophecies she has studied. Eugene admits that this prophecy has escaped his reading and asks her to take the lead. Olokun offers her the choice of pointing out the way without accompanying them. She answers that she must come because they do not know the route.

As they enter a valley, she tells them about Vasatzi Alavara. In Liora’s account, Vasatzi was raised under a prophecy requiring a sacrifice on her fiftieth birthday. The sacrifice has already happened. Liora says its aftermath has left Vasatzi enraged at the existence imposed upon her, and that this anger is connected to the destruction within the peaks.

Gudlaug asks the practical question: if the prophecy has already been fulfilled, why have they been summoned? Liora’s answer changes the mission from fulfilling a prediction to approaching its victim. She wants the company to help put Vasatzi at ease.

What the guide has held back

Some of the travelers sense that Liora is reluctant to tell them everything. Asked about the recurring number five, she explains her belief that Vasatzi’s life force has been divided among five ancient artifacts scattered through the mountains.

Her plan is to gather these fragments and perform a ritual at the heart of Vasatzi’s power. She believes reuniting them can restore a sense of wholeness and bring peace. The same objects could also be used to destroy Vasatzi. Recovering them therefore gives their holders a dangerous choice.

The party does not accept that choice without questioning it. Eugene asks why someone who hates her existence should not be helped to end it, and whether she has any agency over her destiny. Gudlaug asks what would happen if the artifacts fell into the wrong hands. Olokun suggests finding them and reaching a decision with Vasatzi herself. Liora continues to argue for saving her.

These are the guide’s explanations and hopes. The shaking ground is observable; the full history, the artifacts’ ultimate powers and the proposed ritual’s success are not independently proved by her confidence.

The rockfall splits the company

The narrow pass begins to shake. Liora shouts for cover as cracks spread through the cliffs and stone falls toward the path. A huge boulder blocks the route, leaving travelers on opposite sides.

Danger approaches from the north while the southern group initially sees only the obstruction between them and their companions. Gudlaug throws Olokun into the air, giving him a view of enormous creatures moving through the peaks to the southeast. The company must respond to threats it cannot all see from the same position.

A frosty beast advances and attacks Uthgar. The boulder is eventually split, but its fragments still obstruct movement. Another immense creature emerges from the mountains. Clearing the way does not clear the danger.

Leo finds the first artifact

After the fighting, a pulsing blue light draws attention to a crack in the mountainside. Leo approaches, and the light becomes easier to see. Liora identifies what he finds as one of the objects they came to recover.

Leo promises to keep it in sight. Liora tells him that it will be necessary for her ritual, then urges the party onward. She also warns a traveler about coming into these mountains without suitable clothing. The mission now combines a fragile object in the party’s care with exposure, difficult terrain and a guide who expects the conditions to worsen.

Liora interprets each disturbance as a sign that they are approaching another artifact. That interpretation gives the company a way to read its route, while leaving it dependent on her account of what the mountain’s violence means.

A tornado uncovers another fragment

The next pass is narrow, littered with jagged stone and increasingly dark beneath gathering clouds. The wind changes, and a column of debris forms ahead. The tornado tears through the path, breaking stone and throwing it into the air.

The travelers take shelter where they can. When the wind finally moves on, they emerge onto a route more damaged than before. Among the fresh rubble lies another light, flickering purple and blue. Liora calls it the second discovery and says that three remain.

The find comes from the destruction they have just survived. It is an immediate advance in the search, but it gives them no reason to treat the weather as harmless or the remaining journey as assured.

The account of Vasatzi changes

Liora apologizes for not being more forthcoming. She describes Vasatzi as betrayed by the people who raised her to accept the sacrifice and then forced its consequences upon her. What Liora first presented as a fulfilled duty becomes, in her later account, a story of lost humanity, resentment and imposed power.

Olokun finds that anger understandable even while recognizing the danger it creates. He still wants to try reasoning with her. The company is carrying on toward a person whose wishes are being interpreted for them, while some of its members have already questioned whether reconciliation is what that person wants.

Into the blizzard

The temperature falls as the route opens out. Scribonia and Leo recognize the signs of an approaching blizzard. Liora begins a story about Vasatzi helping villagers through a harsh winter, but the worsening snow interrupts her before she can finish it.

Within minutes, the company is in a whiteout. The path disappears, visibility falls to a few feet, and creatures begin to surround the travelers as silhouettes in the snow. Moving and fighting become harder. Liora herself can no longer see clearly.

During the battle, a dead, cracked ice creature begins to glow from within. Uthgar raises his axe toward the light. The narration establishes the glow, but does not identify it in that moment as a recovered third artifact. That distinction matters: Liora has counted two finds; the company has now encountered another phenomenon that still needs explanation.

Shelter before answers

Liora urgently calls for cover. A small, secluded cave is spotted through the storm, offering somewhere the company can take refuge. The recovered stage ends with the search still underway, its travelers battered by creatures and weather and still dependent on one another.

They have reached the peaks, questioned the guide’s purpose, survived the broken pass and tornado, and recovered two objects Liora identifies as parts of the proposed ritual. They have also learned that her first explanation left out the coercion in Vasatzi’s story. The checked scene does not establish collection of all five artifacts, a meeting with Vasatzi, or completion of the ritual. Those missing outcomes cannot be supplied by turning the expedition’s opening into a triumphant ending.

People and places in this history Liora Fenwick · Olokun · Scribonia · Eugene
